topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatment.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatment and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain established approaches to eliminating tumors and the practical limitations of treating cancer without cancer-specific molecular targeting.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how continued dependence on hormonal signals provides a selective treatment opportunity.

topics.label: Exploiting defective cell cycle checkpoints
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how loss of checkpoint proteins creates vulnerabilities that treatments can exploit selectively in cancer cells.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking an additional DNA repair pathway selectively kills cells already deficient in BRCA-mediated repair.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the strategy of inhibiting cancer-driving oncogenes through its molecular basis and the complications that limit sustained treatment success.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeting of cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognizing cancer cell surface proteins direct therapeutic activity toward those cells.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic evaluates whether naturally occurring immune responses protect against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint blockade and tumor recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the effectiveness and limitations of reactivating T cells that recognize tumor antigens.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapies that deliberately connect T cell cytotoxic activity to selected cancer cell antigens.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided selection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the difficulty of matching effective treatments to individual patients as cancers vary and evolve.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic assesses how prevention and earlier detection contribute to observed improvements in cancer outcomes.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how future treatment development must balance potential improvements against the benefits and burdens of established care.
